The whole molecule likely is benzophenone? Wait formula C13H10O: benzaldehyde is C7H6O, not. Phenyl phenyl ketone (benzophenone) is C13H10O? Actually benzophenone formula C13H10O? Let's check: benzophenone = diphenyl ketone, C13H10O? Each phenyl C6H5, two phenyl = C12H10, plus carbonyl carbon O = C13H10O. Yes. So benzophenone has 13 carbons, 10 hydrogens, one oxygen carbonyl, aromatic carbons 12 (two phenyl rings). No methyl groups. Unique carbon environments: In benzophenone, there are 5 distinct carbon types: carbonyl carbon, two sets of equivalent aromatic carbons: the ipso carbons attached to carbonyl (two equivalent), the ortho carbons (four equivalent), meta (four), para (two). That's 5 types. Unique hydrogen environment: all aromatic hydrogens are equivalent? In benzophenone, hydrogens on both rings are chemically equivalent due to symmetry? Actually the two phenyl rings are equivalent, and within each ring, positions relative to carbonyl are same across both rings, so all 10 hydrogens are equivalent. So 1 hydrogen environment matches. So SMILES for benzophenone: O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2 . Or "O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2". Could also be "O=C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1". That's same. Provide SMILES string.

Thus final answer: O=C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1
